sample_unit: CT report cases rated by clinicians (disagreement cases)
models_evaluated: seven LLMs built on a CT-CLIP encoder

links.outcome: Validity of report-generation evaluation metrics against expert ratings and under style or error perturbation
links.effect: Lexical NLG metrics highly sensitive to stylistic variation; GREEN Score best aligned with experts (Spearman~0.70); CRG negatively correlated; BERTScore-F1 least sensitive to factual error injection.
links.quote: Using our novel framework, we found that lexical NLG metrics are highly sensitive to stylistic variations; GREEN Score aligns best with expert judgments (Spearman~0.70), while CRG shows negative correlation; and BERTScore-F1 is least sensitive to factual error injection.

unlisted_practices: Validating automated radiology report-generation metrics against clinician ratings, style rephrasing, and synthetic error injection before relying on them for quality assessment

screen.reason: The study develops and empirically evaluates a validation framework (stress testing via style variation, synthetic error injection, and clinician correlation) to assess the clinical validity and safety of automated evaluation metrics used for generative radiology reporting.

primary.practice: automated metric evaluation framework for radiology report validation
